summary: Add a group_by function, so an array of objects can be split into groups by a string key in one expression.
behaviour: `group_by(array, &expr)` returns an object with one key per distinct value of `expr` over the elements. Each key maps to an array of the elements with that key, in their original order, and the keys appear in the order they first occur.
The key of an element must be a string. Elements whose key is null are left out; any other type of key (number, boolean, array or object) raises `JMESPathTypeError`.
An empty array gives an empty object `{}`.
The first argument must be an array; anything else raises `JMESPathTypeError`, as for `sort_by`.

entries: - Fixed: min_by and max_by raise JMESPathTypeError, not TypeError, when the keys mix numbers and strings. (feature/0b71e4)
- Fixed: merge() builds its result with the dict_cls given in Options, like the rest of a search. (feature/2e6f48)

entry: - Added: A group_by function that groups the elements of an array by a string key. ({branch})

main_commits.message: Make min_by and max_by require keys of one type, like sort_by
Build merge() results with the dict_cls from Options
